---
title: "The `RoomAdventure` Class"
---

Now let's build the `RoomAdventure` class. This is the main class that drives the game. At the very top of the file, **before the class declaration**, add the import statement for the `Scanner` class. The `Scanner` will be used to take input from the user.

```java
import java.util.Scanner;
```

Then begin the class just below it:

```java
class RoomAdventure {

}
```

## Class Variables

The game needs several pieces of state that every method in the class can access. In Java, variables that are shared across all methods in a class (without needing an object instance) are declared with the `static` keyword.

Add these class variables inside `RoomAdventure`:

```java
private static Room currentRoom;

private static String[] inventory = {null, null, null, null, null};

private static String status;
```

- `currentRoom` tracks which room the player is currently in.
- `inventory` is a fixed-size array of 5 strings. Each slot starts as `null`. `null` is Java's equivalent of Python's `None`. A consideration as part of your game enhancements would be to make the inventory more dynamic instead of being limited to 5 items. 
- `status` holds the message that gets printed after each command is processed.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Python Comparison
Python class variables are declared directly in the class body (outside any method). Java uses the `static` keyword to achieve the same effect. Both are shared across the class without needing to create an instance.
:::

## Constants

A variable declared with the `final` keyword in Java cannot be reassigned after it is first set. The keyword `final` means it is a constant. By convention, constants are named in `ALL_CAPS_WITH_UNDERSCORES` (also known as `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`).

Add the `DEFAULT_STATUS` constant below the class variables:

```java
final private static String DEFAULT_STATUS = "Sorry. I did not understand. Try [verb] [noun].";
```

This is the error message displayed whenever the player does not type exactly two words.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Python Comparison
Python has no built-in constant keyword. Developers use `ALL_CAPS` as a naming convention to signal "do not change this." Java enforces it with `final`. The compiler will reject any attempt to reassign a `final` variable.
:::

## Where We Are So Far

The top of your file should now look like this:

```java
import java.util.Scanner;

class RoomAdventure {

    private static Room currentRoom;
    private static String[] inventory = {null, null, null, null, null};
    private static String status;

    final private static String DEFAULT_STATUS = "Sorry. I did not understand. Try [verb] [noun].";

    // methods will go here

}
```

In the next sections you will add the methods one at a time.
